svg.aria-label: Four scenarios on the path client, CDN, web servers and load balancer, application tier, data tier; the client and the web servers form the presentation tier. Web servers fail: the load balancer routes around the failed web server, the other web servers absorb the traffic with little user-visible impact, and auto-scaling replaces the failed instance. Application tier fails: the load balancer routes around the failed application server, the other instances continue processing requests, and auto-scaling replaces the failed instance. Data tier fails: the application tier cannot read or write data, requests fail or degrade, use replication, automatic failover or read replicas. CDN or delivery tier fails: once DNS points at the origin, static content is served directly from origin servers with higher latency; until DNS is repointed, traffic does not reach the application
svg.text: Fault tolerance: what happens when a tier fails?
Each row fails one tier on the same request path and shows the effect and the fix.
The load balancer routes around the failed web server.
Other web servers absorb the traffic, with little user-visible impact.
The load balancer routes around the failed application server.
Application tier cannot read or write data.
Requests fail or return degraded responses.
Use replication, automatic failover, or read replicas.
Static content is served directly from origin servers once DNS points at the origin.
Until DNS is repointed, traffic does not reach the application.
